message.content:
**Founder:**  
Buddhism was founded by **Siddhartha Gautama**, who is commonly known as **the Buddha** (the “Enlightened One”).

**Origin:**  
The Buddha was born in the **ancient Indian subcontinent**—specifically in the region that is today part of **Lumbini, Nepal** (though his early life and teachings were centered in what is now northern India). The tradition of Buddhism began there around the **5th–4th centuries BCE**. From this birthplace, the Buddha’s teachings spread throughout India and eventually across Asia.

According to common knowledge, Buddhism was founded by Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) in ancient India, specifically in the region of Lumbini (modern Nepal) or in the area of present-day India. The origin is in ancient India, around 5th century BCE. So answer: Siddhartha Gautama, also known as the Buddha, founded Buddhism in ancient India, in the region of Lumbini (modern Nepal) or in the area of present-day India. Provide details.
